growthBrief.opportunityTitle: Vercel's 14-person marketing team has no marketer-owned ABM layer: Prismic Agents close that gap against a $200M ARR growth backdrop.

rationaleBlocks.title: The gap
bullets: Vercel's own marketing site runs on **Next.js + Vercel** but has no observed headless CMS or marketer-owned LP layer, meaning every campaign page change requires an eng PR.
With only **14 marketers** supporting a $200M ARR business in active enterprise expansion, LP iteration throughput is almost certainly the binding constraint on pipeline velocity.
No visible ABM personalisation layer detected on vercel.com: named-account visitors see a generic homepage, a direct mismatch with their new enterprise sales motion.
Vercel integrates with Contentful, Sanity, and Storyblok per their docs, suggesting **no committed CMS vendor**: the slot is open and the timing is ideal.

rationaleBlocks.title: The math
bullets: Rough ACV assumption: **EUR 300K/yr** enterprise tier (comparable developer-platform deals at this scale), implying EUR 25K/month recognised.
Expansion path: Prismic ABM Agent, SEO Agent, Paid Ads Agent, and Localization Agent each add roughly **EUR 1-3K/month** per activated module.

If Vercel's enterprise push adds 20+ named accounts per quarter needing bespoke LPs, the cost of eng-gated iteration (eng salary, delay, lost conversion) conservatively exceeds **EUR 10K/month** in opportunity cost alone.
Total opportunity estimate: **EUR 28K/month** blended (licence + agents), conservative against a company growing ARR at 82% YoY.

rationaleBlocks.title: Why now
bullets: Vercel hired a **CMO (Keith Messick)** from Redis and is explicitly building out an enterprise sales motion: ABM infrastructure demand is imminent.
The **WPP partnership** and TISAX AL2 compliance signal regulated-industry and agency verticals opening up, both requiring localised, compliant LP variants at scale.
Next.js ecosystem lock-in is a **tailwind, not a risk**: Prismic Slice Machine is the only headless CMS with native Next.js slice architecture, making the pitch a zero-migration story.
Competitor Netlify is actively targeting the non-developer marketer segment; Vercel risks ceding marketer mindshare without a CMS answer.

rationaleBlocks.title: What Prismic Agents ship
bullets: **ABM Agent**: reverse-IP detection auto-serves named-account LP variants within hours of account list upload, no eng involvement.
**SEO Agent**: audits and rewrites meta, headings, and structured data on every LP at publish time, compounding organic acquisition.
**Paid Ads Agent**: aligns LP copy to Google and LinkedIn ad group intent signals, reducing CPC waste and lifting Quality Score.
**Localization Agent**: spins up translated variants for EU and APAC markets Vercel is expanding into, supporting the global enterprise GTM.

quickWins.text: **Send** a Prismic-built, Vercel-branded ABM demo page (featuring their Next.js stack) to Keith Messick's team this week and **measure** reply rate as primary signal.
**Gate** a live 15-minute build session showing Slice Machine deploying to Vercel CI/CD with zero eng involvement, targeting the marketing ops or web lead directly.
**Run** a reverse-IP audit on vercel.com traffic to identify top 20 enterprise visitors receiving no personalisation, then **share** the named-account gap report as a cold outbound hook.

**Build** a comparison LP: Prismic plus Next.js versus Contentful plus Next.js, benchmarking marketer autonomy and time-to-publish, and **track** organic SEO traffic to that page as a pipeline signal.

**Activate** a Localization Agent demo targeting Vercel's EU and APAC expansion markets (DE, JP, SG) to show localised LP variants auto-generated from a single English Slice, and **measure** stakeholder engagement from their international GTM team.
